transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... I guess the main reason I’m here is that I've been struggling just a little bit at work lately. I manage health services, which I usually really enjoy, but I've noticed that anything that takes, well, real sitting-down brain work? Like doing the big monthly reports, or trying to plan out a multi-site health event... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

I end up putting those things off, even when I know they really matter and people are counting on me. I know everyone procrastinates sometimes, so maybe it's just a normal bad habit I need to work on, but... I just wanted to get your thoughts on it, if that's okay? Does that make sense as a reason to come in?
Were these kinds of attention or procrastination problems present when you were a child or teenager?

Um, well... I guess if I really think back, maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a good kid, I never caused any trouble or anything like that. But, um... I suppose even back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents that I was bright, but that I tended to daydream a lot. 

I guess I did have a bit of a habit of misplacing my worksheets, or... well, sometimes I'd forget to turn in my homework. It wasn't that I didn't want to do it! It's just... I'd only really remember if my mom checked my backpack every night to make sure everything was in order. I know a lot of kids are a little scatterbrained like that, though, right? So I don't know if that's exactly what you're looking for, but... does that answer your question?
Do you often avoid social situations because you worry people will criticize you or reject you?

Oh, um... no, not really. I actually really enjoy being around people. I mean, I hope I'm well-liked! I try hard to be a good colleague and friend, and I don't really sit around worrying that people are going to judge me or reject me. 

I definitely don't avoid social things. Honestly, talking with people and collaborating is usually the part of my day I feel the most comfortable with. I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for, but... yeah, I'd say I'm pretty okay on the social front. Is it okay that I don't have that issue?
When you were a child, did you also have trouble staying seated or felt unusually fidgety compared with other kids?

Um, no, I don't think so. I was actually a pretty quiet kid, to be honest. I really never wanted to be a bother to my teachers, so I always made sure to stay in my seat and follow the rules. 

I wasn't really the type to bounce off the walls or, you know, run around when I wasn't supposed to. I think I was more just... quietly off in my own world, if that makes sense? I hope that's okay, that I didn't have the fidgety stuff. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here. Is that helpful at all?
Have these work difficulties started only after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Well, um... I guess it kind of did start around a specific time. I mean, I've always been a little disorganized, but... it really got harder to manage about, oh, maybe a year and 11 months ago? 

I went through a bit of a tough time... a good friend of mine passed away. It was, you know, it was hard. And around that same time, I stepped up to take on more responsibilities with our local league and some outreach stuff. I just wanted to help out, you know? Be a good team player. But I think maybe all of that extra on my plate, plus dealing with the loss... it just made it harder to keep all the balls in the air at work. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses! I know I should be able to handle it all. But... yeah, I suppose that's when things really started to slip. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not oversharing or anything.
Do you have these concentration and organization problems outside of work too, such as at home or in other parts of your life?

Well, um... I guess it does spill over a little bit, yeah. I mean, I'm still getting by, you know? I'm keeping my job, and I'm still involved in the community stuff. I try really hard not to let anyone down. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, I think some people have had to cover a few gaps for me lately. Just small things! And, well, a few deadlines at work have slipped past me, which I feel terrible about. I've had to make some pretty embarrassing last-minute apologies to my coworkers, and even to some friends when I've forgotten things we planned. 

I really hate being that guy who always has to say "I'm sorry, I forgot," you know? I want people to know they can rely on me. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely falling apart, because I'm really trying my best to keep it all together. Is it normal for it to affect things at home and with friends like that?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things most days, and is it hard to control that worry?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier, exactly. I definitely don't sit around agonizing over things all day. 

I mean, sure, I want to do a good job, and I care about what people think, so I might double-check an email or, you know, hope a meeting goes well. But I don't feel like I'm out of control with it or anything like that. I think I'm just pretty normal when it comes to that stuff, just wanting to be conscientious and responsible. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't think anxiety or worrying is really my main issue, if that makes sense.
Before the loss of your friend about two years ago, did you have these attention or organization problems consistently, or were they mainly something that started after that time?

Well, um... I guess if I really look back, it wasn't just after my friend passed. I've always been a little... well, maybe scattered is the right word? 

I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything! I always tried hard to please my teachers. But, um, even back in elementary school, they would tell my parents that I was bright, which was nice to hear, but... they also said I was always daydreaming. I would lose worksheets a lot, or just completely forget to turn in my homework. 

Honestly, I think I only got by because my mom would check my backpack every single night to make sure I had everything. It's a little embarrassing to admit that, honestly. I should have been able to keep track of my own things, right? I just... I don't want you to think I'm lazy or anything. I've always wanted to do things right, it just took a lot of extra help when I was younger. Does that help answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most days?

Oh, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I mess up at work or forget something, but... I definitely don't feel hopeless or depressed. 

I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? I have a good life and I'm really grateful for it. I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around complaining, because I'm really not an unhappy person. I just want to get better at managing my day-to-day stuff so I can be at my best for everyone at the clinic and at home. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you, but mood-wise, I think I'm doing okay.
How much are these attention and organization problems actually interfering with your work or daily life?

Well, um... I mean, I'm still getting by, you know? I haven't lost my job or anything drastic like that. I really try to keep things running smoothly. 

But, I guess... if I'm being completely honest... it is causing some hiccups. Like, I've missed a few deadlines recently. Nothing that ruined the clinic, but... enough that other people have had to step in and cover the gaps for me. Which is awful, because I really pride myself on being a team player. I hate feeling like I'm letting my coworkers down. 

And, um, outside of work, it's a little embarrassing, but I've had to make some last-minute apologies to friends because I completely forgot about plans we made, or I double-booked myself. I just... I try so hard to be reliable, and it's really frustrating when I fall short. I don't want anyone to think I don't care about them or my job. 

Is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I'm just trying to give you the full picture.
Before age 12, did your teachers or parents ever say you had trouble paying attention or staying focused?

Well, um... I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, but... I don't really remember them saying I had trouble paying attention, exactly. I mean, they said I was a daydreamer, like I mentioned before, but they always made sure to say I was a good kid and very bright. 

I think... well, I was pretty quiet, so I wasn't disrupting the class or anything like that. I always wanted to be good for the teachers. I don't recall anyone sitting my parents down and saying I couldn't focus, just... maybe that my head was in the clouds sometimes. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to give you the impression I was a problem student, because I always tried my best to do what I was told. Does that answer your question okay?
Did these attention and organization problems clearly start before you were 12 years old?

Well, yes, I suppose they did. Um, like I mentioned a minute ago, the teachers always made sure to tell my parents I was bright—which I really appreciated, I always wanted them to be proud of me. But, looking back... yeah, even in elementary school, along with the daydreaming, there were some other little issues. 

I, um... I guess I had a bad habit of losing my worksheets. And I'd forget to turn in my homework. Actually, if I'm being completely honest, my mother had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure my assignments actually made it back to the teacher the next day. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit that she had to hold my hand like that, but she was just being a really supportive mom, you know? I wasn't trying to be defiant or anything, I just... things would sort of slip my mind. I hope I'm not painting too bad a picture of myself as a kid. Does that give you what you need for the timeline?
